title: In my RPG your lantern is the best and worst thing you carry
author: zanemoore575
selftext:
I've been making Nightfall, a slow, story-driven dark fantasy RPG. You go into a ruined holy city full of the dead, take what you can, and try to get back out alive. I want to talk about the one item I've spent more time on than anything else: the lantern on your belt.

The whole game hangs on one rule: **the dead are drawn to light, and light burns them.**

The Light raised them. They still want it, and it still hurts them.

So when you light up, you can see. Anything fighting you in your light is weaker, and the Paladin gets his mana back faster. But every sleeper on the street wakes from about three times further off.

With the lantern out, most of the dead stay where they are: sitting at tables, slumped in doorways, eyes faintly glowing. But whatever you do wake hits harder in the dark, and in pitch black you can only see a few metres.

Lighting it is deliberate. Your knight raises the lantern, and for a few seconds you're open. Putting it out is instant, one sweep of the shield. 

That difference turned out to be the most fun part. Going dark is your best way to escape: lose the dead in the dark and they search where they last saw you, then give up and go back where they were.

The moment that sold me on it: on one street a household is still sitting at supper, faces turned up to their own lantern on the table. Walk past dark and only their eyes move. Walk past lit and all four get up from their chairs.

The night makes it harder as it goes. A raid runs on six bells, and the clouds cover more of the moon at each bell. At the fourth bell the old lamps that have burned since the city fell go out, the dead rise, and from then on a lit lantern draws them from much further away. By the fifth bell the moon is gone, and your lantern is the brightest thing in the city. 

**Light keeps you alive in a fight, and it brings the fight to you.** 

The Mage plays it differently. She can light a candle she can see from across the street, and the dead nearby can’t help but to wander over to it.

**0.3.1 just went up on itch,** with QoL improvements and quest updates. A bigger map and the third raid are to come a future release; they're still being built. 

Fair warning: it's tab-target, and it's hard. Two of the dead at once can put a new character down, and running away is a real plan.

[https://middafrostey.itch.io/nightfall](https://middafrostey.itch.io/nightfall)

I'm curious how other people feel about light as something you manage in an RPG. Do you like having to choose, or does it just get in the way of smashing stuff?
